A confrontation between a couple and a food influencer outside a San Francisco coffee shop has gone viral after the content creator posted a video of the spat online this week.

On Tuesday afternoon, food influencer Allie Tong was filming a video outside the Wrecking Ball Coffee when a man and women nearby began getting irritated.

According to Tong, an older man started muttering “you guys are so f—king stupid” at her assistant, to which Tong walked back to the man and asked what he said.

He repeated his insult, despite Tong stating the she and her assistant were supporting a small local business. That’s when the assistant began filming the couple, “because he was being verbally abusive,” Tong said.

At the beginning of the video, the camera panned over to a couple drinking their coffee, when the woman suddenly lunged at the assistant to seemingly knock the camera away.

“Don’t touch me!” “What’s wrong with you?” the two can be heard exchanging.

The woman then started marching toward the assistant, who began walking backward with a coffee in hand.

“I was just filming because he was making us feel uncomfortable,” the assistant can be heard trying to explain to the furious woman. “Get off of me,” the assistant said repeatedly.

A post shared by Allie Tong | Food + Recipes (@allie.eats)

“Take that recording and delete it,” the woman demanded.

Later, the woman can be seen with the assistant’s sunglasses as the couple appeared to leave the scene. The man then uttered another insult as while walking by.

“You want this?” the angry woman tauneds before leaving with the glasses. “Call the police. Let’s call the police right now.”

The clip garnered tens of thousands of views, and Wrecking Ball swiftly banned the couple from the coffee shop.

“Wrecking Ball has always been committed to providing a safe, friendly and welcoming environment for everyone and we take that responsibility very seriously,” Wrecking Ball Coffee co-owner Joey Cannata told the San Francisco Chronicle.

In a Wednesday update, Tong said the assistant did get her sunglasses back because the lady eventually threw them on the ground.

The San Francisco Police Department confirmed to the Chronicle that a police report was filed but no arrest has been made.

The couple has not been publicly identified.

زن خواست: «آن ضبط را بردارید و حذف کنید.» بعداً، زن با عینک آفتابی دستیار در حالی که زوج ظاهر می‌شوند دیده می‌شود.

Southern California’s Halloween festivities could turn into a soggy mess as a powerful storm threatens to drench trick-or-treaters, unleash thunderstorms and deliver the region’s first rainy Oct. 31 in years.

The spooky weather system is expected to sweep across the Southland Saturday evening, bringing widespread rainfall just as costumed children hit the streets in search of candy.

Los Angeles could experience its first wet Halloween since 2014, putting a damper on a holiday that has largely escaped rain for more than a decade.

And Mother Nature isn’t waiting until Halloween night to make her presence known.

Scattered showers began creeping into parts of Southern California Friday morning, offering an ominous preview of the heavier downpours expected to arrive over the weekend.

The National Weather Service warned that the storm’s most significant rainfall will likely coincide with peak trick-or-treating hours Saturday night before intensifying overnight into Sunday.

Forecasters expect widespread rainfall totals between half an inch and 1.5 inches, with some mountain and foothill communities potentially getting soaked with as much as 2.5 inches.

“This has been a challenging system to get a hold of and even more challenging to describe,” the National Weather Service said in its forecast discussion.

The agency warned that rainfall predictions remain uncertain, with a 20% chance that some areas could receive either double or half the currently projected amounts.

The storm is being fueled by a collision between chilly northern air and a surge of moisture moving into the region from the southwest.

“This upper-level low is going to pick up all the moisture related to this system down to our southwest, and all that moisture is clashing with the colder air to the north,” FOX 11 meteorologist Maria Quiban explained.

That atmospheric clash could also produce a frightening addition to Halloween night — thunder and lightning.

Forecasters estimate a 10% to 20% chance of isolated thunderstorms Saturday night into early Sunday, particularly across southern portions of the region.

“If you are headed out to trick-or-treat, make sure you have your umbrella and, of course, rain boots,” Quiban warned.

Temperatures are also expected to take a tumble, with daytime highs hovering in the upper 60s to low 70s under mostly cloudy skies.

Saturday morning and early afternoon should offer a brief reprieve for families hoping to squeeze in Halloween festivities before the storm arrives.

Most areas will see only scattered sprinkles during the day, with rainfall accumulations generally staying below one-tenth of an inch.

But conditions are expected to deteriorate after sunset.

San Bernardino could receive around an inch of rain, while Woodland Hills and Burbank may see approximately four-tenths of an inch, according to Quiban.

Santa Clarita could receive slightly more, while Palm Springs may also get drenched with nearly an inch.

The National Weather Service’s San Diego office issued its own Halloween-themed warning on X.

“A spooky storm system will move through the region Halloween night into Sunday morning,” the agency wrote. “Widespread rain is expected with the heaviest rain in SD County.”

Meanwhile, coastal communities are facing a separate weather headache.

A coastal flood advisory remains in effect through 2 p.m. Friday for beaches in Los Angeles, Orange and Ventura counties, where elevated tides and surf reaching 4 to 5 feet could trigger minor flooding.

High tides between 6 and 7 feet are expected Friday morning, although forecasters say coastal flooding should be less severe than earlier in the week.

The Halloween storm is expected to gradually lose its grip on Southern California Sunday morning, with most rainfall clearing out by the afternoon.

A weak high-pressure system should usher in warmer, drier conditions early next week, giving residents a chance to dry out their costumes and recover from the soggy holiday.

Another cooling trend could arrive toward the end of next week, although additional rainfall currently appears unlikely.
news.content: پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. جشن های هالووین کالیفرنیای جنوبی می تواند به یک آشفتگی خیس تبدیل شود زیرا یک طوفان قدرتمند تهدید می کند افراد حقه باز را خیس می کند، رعد و برق را راه می اندازد و اولین 31 اکتبر بارانی منطقه در سال های اخیر را به ارمغان می آورد. انتظار می رود که سیستم آب و هوای شبح آور، حتی در حالی که روز شنبه باران های جنوبی را فرا می گیرد، همه جا را فرا خواهد گرفت. بچه های لباس پوشیده در جستجوی آب نبات به خیابان ها می روند. لس آنجلس می تواند اولین هالووین خیس خود را از سال 2014 تجربه کند و در تعطیلاتی که بیش از یک دهه است تا حد زیادی از باران در امان مانده است، دمپری ایجاد کند. و مادر طبیعت منتظر نیست تا شب هالووین حضور خود را نشان دهد. بارش های پراکنده در بخش هایی از جنوب کالیفرنیا صبح جمعه شروع به خزیدن کردند و پیش نمایشی شوم از پایان هفته را به او ارائه کردند. سرویس ملی هواشناسی هشدار داد که مهم‌ترین بارندگی طوفان احتمالاً همزمان با ساعات اوج ترفند شنبه شب قبل از تشدید در شب تا یکشنبه خواهد بود. پیش‌بینی‌کنندگان انتظار دارند که بارندگی گسترده بین نیم اینچ تا 1.5 اینچ باشد و برخی از مناطق کوهستانی و کوهپایه‌ای احتمالاً تا 2.5 اینچ خیس شوند. سرویس ملی هواشناسی در بحث پیش‌بینی خود گفت: «این یک سیستم چالش‌برانگیز برای دستیابی به آن بوده است و حتی توصیف آن چالش‌برانگیزتر بوده است.» این آژانس هشدار داد که پیش‌بینی‌های بارندگی نامشخص باقی می‌مانند، با احتمال 20 درصد که برخی مناطق می‌توانند دو برابر شوند.

People Inc., the publishing giant behind People magazine, is laying off 195 employees — roughly 6% of its workforce — with most of the cuts hitting its print and legacy web businesses, according to an internal memo obtained by The Post.

Chief Executive Neil Vogel told staff that the company has hired 320 employees so far this year and plans to continue making investments in 2027 despite the latest cuts.

“The rapid changes in media are evident to us all, and require us to be constantly changing as well,” Vogel wrote in the memo.

“We have significantly increased investments in a host of new projects as we continue to align the company with our biggest opportunities.”

Human resources and managers have scheduled one-on-one meetings with employees affected by the cuts.

The cuts come amid a broader overhaul at the publisher, which changed its name from Dotdash Meredith to People Inc. in July of last year.

Its roster of magazines also includes Better Homes & Gardens, Food & Wine, Real Simple, Southern Living, Travel + Leisure and EatingWell.

Its parent company, IAC, which is chaired by media mogul Barry Diller, renamed itself People Incorporated in June 2026 as it sharpened its focus on the publishing business.

The parent remains a separate legal entity from the publisher, whose legal name is People Inc. Group.

In October 2025, People Inc. axed 226 employees, or roughly 6% of its workforce, as Vogel sought to redirect investments toward social media publishing, commerce, events and businesses less dependent on traditional website traffic.

That followed the elimination of 143 jobs in January 2025 and 53 positions in November 2024, when the company cited continued weakness in print advertising.

The publisher had previously slashed 274 jobs in January 2023.

The restructuring comes as People Inc. grapples with declining print revenue and falling web traffic, which the company has attributed primarily to Google’s AI-powered search summaries.

In the second quarter of 2026, print revenue tumbled 16% from a year earlier to $132.6 million, while digital revenue climbed 6% to $289.9 million, according to company filings.

Traffic to the company’s core digital properties plunged 22% from a year earlier, a decline the publisher attributed primarily to Google’s AI Overviews, which can answer search queries without directing users to outside websites.

Licensing and other digital revenue rose 23% in the second quarter, while performance marketing revenue increased 13%, according to company filings.

Despite the layoffs, Vogel pointed to continued hiring at the company.

“We’ve added 320 new employees so far in 2026, expanding our talent and capabilities across the company, and we plan to continue making meaningful investments in 2027,” he wrote.

Vogel said the company would hold an all-hands meeting after announcing third-quarter earnings to discuss its direction and priorities for next year.

The Post has sought comment from People Inc.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Credit card bills have a way of piling up. A few unexpected expenses, a stretch of higher living costs or a temporary loss of income can leave households juggling multiple payments while interest charges eat away at their budgets.

A recent survey by Achieve shows that 43% of survey respondents say they have felt hopeless about their financial situation due to debt. Getting out of debt can be harder than getting into it. When much of your monthly payment goes toward interest instead of reducing what you owe, even people who have cut their spending can struggle to make progress.

Fortunately, there are ways to take control of debt without resorting to drastic measures. From choosing the right repayment strategy to consolidating balances or getting professional help, these seven approaches can make debt more manageable and potentially save thousands of dollars in interest.

The starting point for any debt repayment plan is a complete inventory of your outstanding debts. A bunch of papers on your desk won’t do it, however; first, set up a spreadsheet that compiles your credit card statements, personal loan documents, medical bills and other debts.

For each account, record the outstanding balance, annual percentage rate (APR), minimum monthly payment and payment due date. The APR is a key metric because it measures your annual cost of borrowing and helps identify what debts are costing you the most.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) recommends using a debt reduction worksheet and bill calendar to organize payments and develop a repayment strategy. Having everything in one place also makes it easier to identify bills that might otherwise be overlooked.

Once you have a single source of truth for your budget, it’s time to calculate how much money remains after you have paid for housing, food, transportation and other necessary expenses. That figure determines how much you can realistically put toward debt repayment beyond the required minimum payments.

Missing a minimum payment can trigger late fees, damage your credit history and potentially cause your interest rate to increase. Keeping every account current should take priority over accelerating payments on any single debt.

The debt snowball method is a debt repayment strategy popularized by Dave Ramsey that focuses on paying off your smallest balances first, regardless of their interest rates. The goal is to eliminate individual debts quickly and build your confidence as you see the number of your outstanding accounts shrink.

Using the debt snowball, you make the minimum required payment on every account, then direct any additional money toward the debt with the smallest balance. When that debt is eliminated, apply the money you were paying toward it to the next-smallest balance.

Suppose you owe $500 on one credit card, $2,000 on another and $7,000 on a third. Under the snowball method, you would attack the $500 balance first, even if the larger debts carry higher interest rates.

The advantage of this approach is psychological. Eliminating a debt account is like tidying your house: Once you see how much better it looks with one clean room, you feel motivated to tackle more difficult projects.

The downside of this approach is that it’s more expensive in the long run. For borrowers who care more about minimizing interest than celebrating quick victories, the debt avalanche method offers a different approach.

Rather than ranking debts by balance, the avalanche method prioritizes the account with the highest interest charges (APR). You continue making minimum payments on all other debts while directing extra money toward the most expensive one.

For example, imagine you have three credit cards carrying interest rates of 29%, 24% and 18%. Under the avalanche method, you would pay down the card charging 29% first, regardless of its balance. Once that account is paid off, the additional payments move to the card charging 24%, followed by the card charging 18%.

The math favors this strategy. By reducing the highest-interest balance first, you are reducing the amount of money you will have to pay in the future, assuming your make the same total monthly payments and don’t add new debt.

This approach requires patience. A borrower with a large, high-interest balance might spend months making payments without eliminating a single account.

The Achieve survey shows that a full third of respondents don’t know where to turn to reduce their debt. In these cases, taking control of your finances may not be enough. For example, if your household has experienced a recent reduction in income — especially in the face of rising prices — it may not be possible to put extra money toward paying down debts.

For these households, more involved measures may be necessary. Respondents said consolidating multiple debts with a single personal loan was on the table (48%), followed by working with a debt relief company that negotiates settlements on your behalf (44%), enrolling in a debt management plan via credit counseling (40%) and in the worst case scenario, filing for bankruptcy (21%).

Balance transfer credit cards can provide temporary relief by allowing qualified borrowers to move existing credit card debt onto a new card offering an introductory 0% APR.

Some promotions last 12 months or longer, giving borrowers time to reduce their balances without accumulating additional interest on the transferred amount, but transferring debt isn’t necessarily free. Many balance transfer cards charge an upfront fee, often around 3% to 5% of the amount transferred, even when the promotional interest rate is zero.

However, any balance remaining after the promotional period generally becomes subject to the card’s regular interest rate, and missing payments can also jeopardize promotional terms. Before you sign up for a balance transfer, review the transfer fee, promotional expiration date, purchase APR and minimum payment requirements.

A personal loan offers another way to consolidate expensive credit card debt.

With debt consolidation, a borrower takes out a new loan and uses the proceeds to repay several existing obligations. Instead of managing multiple credit card payments, the borrower makes one monthly payment on the new loan.

Many personal loans have fixed interest rates and repayment schedules. Unlike revolving credit cards, which allow balances to rise and fall as borrowers make purchases and payments, installment loans have scheduled repayment terms.

This can make budgeting easier because borrowers know how much they owe each month and when the loan is scheduled to be paid off.

A consolidation loan may also save money if its APR is lower than the rates on the debts being replaced. However, a lower monthly payment may simply reflect a longer repayment term rather than a reduction in borrowing costs. Equally important, consolidation doesn’t eliminate the underlying cause of debt. Someone who pays off credit cards with a personal loan and then starts charging new purchases could end up owing more than before.

For people who cannot manage their debts independently, nonprofit credit counseling organizations offer another route. Certified credit counselors can review a household’s income, expenses and debts, help develop a budget and evaluate repayment options. Some organizations also administer debt management plans, which establish a structured payment arrangement between borrowers and participating creditors.

Under these plans, the borrower generally makes one monthly payment to the counseling agency. The agency then distributes the money to creditors according to the agreed repayment schedule. Creditors may agree to reduce interest rates, waive certain fees or adjust repayment terms. These concessions can make monthly payments more affordable and help borrowers repay outstanding balances.

Debt management plans may also involve setup or monthly fees. Borrowers should ask whether their creditors participate, whether accounts must be closed and how long repayment is expected to take. The Federal Trade Commission recommends choosing organizations with counselors certified by an outside organization and obtaining written information about fees and services before signing an agreement.

Borrowers should also understand the difference between nonprofit credit counseling and for-profit debt settlement. While credit counseling can help reduce interest rates and adjusting repayment terms, debt settlement companies generally offer to negotiate with creditors to reduce the principal amount owed, allowing consumers to potentially resolve their debts for less than the full balance.While this comes often in exchange for fees, a debt settlement company can only collect fees after successfully negotiating a settlement, the consumer has agreed to it and at least one payment has been made toward that settlement.

Unlike a debt management plan, which seeks to establish affordable repayment terms, settlement attempts to persuade creditors to forgive part of the outstanding balance. During a debt settlement program, consumers typically set aside funds in a dedicated account, which are used to pay settlements as they’re negotiated and approved.

This approach carries risks, however. According to the CFPB, stopping payments can result in additional interest charges, late fees, temporary credit impacts and collection lawsuits. Creditors are not obligated to negotiate with settlement companies, and there is no guarantee that a proposed settlement will succeed. Forgiven debt can also create a tax liability, depending on the borrower’s circumstances and applicable exclusions.

Before paying a settlement company, borrowers can contact their creditors directly to ask about hardship programs, reduced interest rates or alternative payment arrangements. Creditors may be willing to negotiate without involving a third party.

And when debt has become impossible to repay, consulting a qualified debt relief professional or bankruptcy attorney may be more appropriate than spending money on a settlement program to better understand their options and determine which approach fits their financial circumstances.

The most important distinction is whether a proposed solution actually reduces the cost of repayment or merely creates another expense. Borrowers should insist on written terms, calculate the total cost and understand the consequences for their credit before agreeing to any debt relief arrangement.

This article was written by Brooklyn-based financial journalist and Commerce Editor for the New York Post Will Kenton. Specializing in investing, personal finance and retirement planning, Will’s expertise is rooted in behavioral economics — a field he explored as associate editor of the New School Economics Review. Will aims to help readers navigate the “predictable irrationality” that influences financial decisions, providing practical real-world solutions to student loan debt, investments, mortgages and more. Before joining The Post in 2026, Will covered the intersection of money, economics and culture for Investopedia, AP News, Business Insider and TIME Stamped.
news.content: پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. صورتحساب های کارت اعتباری راهی برای انباشته شدن دارند. چند هزینه غیرمنتظره، افزایش هزینه های زندگی یا از دست دادن موقت درآمد می تواند خانوارها را مجبور به پرداخت های متعدد کند در حالی که هزینه های بهره بودجه آنها را از بین می برد. نظرسنجی اخیر توسط Achieve نشان می دهد که 43 درصد از پاسخ دهندگان به نظرسنجی می گویند که از وضعیت مالی خود به دلیل بدهی احساس ناامیدی کرده اند. رهایی از بدهی می تواند سخت تر از وارد شدن به آن باشد. زمانی که بخش عمده ای از پرداخت ماهانه شما به جای کاهش بدهی شما به سمت بهره می رود، حتی افرادی که مخارج خود را کاهش داده اند نیز می توانند پیشرفت کنند. خوشبختانه، راه هایی برای کنترل بدهی ها بدون توسل به اقدامات شدید وجود دارد. از انتخاب استراتژی بازپرداخت مناسب گرفته تا تثبیت مانده‌ها یا دریافت کمک حرفه‌ای، این هفت رویکرد می‌توانند بدهی را قابل مدیریت‌تر کنند و به طور بالقوه هزاران دلار در بهره ذخیره کنند. نقطه شروع هر طرح بازپرداخت بدهی، فهرست کامل بدهی‌های معوق شما است. با این حال، یک دسته کاغذ روی میز شما این کار را نمی کند. ابتدا، صفحه‌گسترده‌ای تنظیم کنید که صورت‌حساب‌های کارت اعتباری، اسناد وام شخصی، صورت‌حساب‌های پزشکی و سایر بدهی‌های شما را گردآوری می‌کند. برای هر حساب، مانده معوقه، نرخ درصد سالانه (APR)، حداقل پرداخت ماهانه و تاریخ سررسید پرداخت را ثبت کنید. APR یک معیار کلیدی است زیرا هزینه سالانه استقراض شما را اندازه گیری می کند و به شناسایی اینکه چه بدهی هایی بیشترین هزینه را برای شما دارد کمک می کند. حفاظت مالی مصرف کننده

Bill Simmons isn’t the most reliable source regarding the Lakers.

On Thursday’s episode of “The Bill Simmons Podcast,” Simmons — a die-hard Celtics fan — claimed, “The Lakers guy doesn’t have the money yet.”

He was referring to Josh Kushner, who bought the Lakers’ franchise from Mark Walter for $12.5 billion in August.

Simmons added, “[Kushner is] still searching for about $5-6 billion of [the money he owes Walter]. Doesn’t have it… [Bob Iger] is putting in the minimum. The minimum is like $63 million. So Kushner has to find all this other money.

“I think they’re using the Buss family as scapegoats for why the deal’s dragging along, but he can’t find the money,” Simmons continued.

Josh Kushner is still $5-6 BILLION short on the Lakers deal and Bob Iger is only putting in "like 63 million dollars," per @BillSimmons "I think they're using the Buss family as scapegoats for why the deal's dragging along, but he can't find the money." pic.twitter.com/pY9tSIc1R4

It turns out Simmons’ claim isn’t completely accurate.

Ben Horney of Front Office Sports reported on Friday, “Josh Kushner and Bob Iger have been offering Lakers minority stakes to investors starting at $250 million apiece as they build out their ownership group.”

Horney added that some investors will put in significantly higher amounts into the deal.

Most importantly, Horney refuted Simmons’ claim that Kushner “can’t find the money,” saying that there has been “massive demand” to get in on the Lakers deal.

Dan Woike of The Athletic confirmed Horney’s report, adding there aren’t any issues finding money for the $12.5 billion sale in an X post on Friday.

It seems Simmons spoke too soon regarding this Lakers deal being in jeopardy.

The resignation of California High-Speed Rail CEO Ian Choudri this week is the latest sign that the project ought to be canceled altogether.

Outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom understood that when he took office in 2019. He told the state legislature in his first “State of the State” address:

“The project, as currently planned, would cost too much and take too long. There’s been too little oversight and not enough transparency.”

“Right now, there simply isn’t a path to get from Sacramento to San Diego, let alone from San Francisco to LA. I wish there were.”

Newsom was right. But he held onto the idea that California could build “a high-speed rail link between Merced and Bakersfield.”

There was never any consumer demand for a passenger link between two rural towns.

California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedInCalifornia Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, XCalifornia Post  Opinion California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!California Post App: Download here!Home delivery: Sign up here!Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!

But there were contractors, and unions, and other special interests who needed to be paid — including the State of California, which wanted to hold onto federal Department of Transportation funding.

So what was once a $33 billion project, to be completed by 2020, ballooned into a $231 billion project covering less than half the distance of the original design.

Choudri wasn’t brought down over billions wasted on a train that has yet to lay a single inch of track. He was forced out over mere hundreds of thousands of dollars in travel expenses for consultants.

The project kept him on, after all, following a domestic violence arrest earlier this year.

It is interesting to note that Choudri lost his job just hours after Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra told a journalist that he was likely to fire Choudri if and when Becerra took office.

So what is really happening is likely political. The California High-Speed Rail Authority is clearly trying to appease the “new sheriff in town,” as Becerra referred to himself in the interview.

The project is trying to save itself by offering Choudri as a sacrificial lamb. It might just work, because Becerra may think he has an excuse to continue funding it, under new leadership.

But the project is so far gone that it doesn’t matter who runs it.

We have more urgent rail challenges in California, like dealing with erosion on the coastal routes between San Diego and LA. Or preventing cargo theft by cartels.

The next governor should cancel the project and use the funding for transportation projects that actually have some prospects of success.

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. استعفای ایان چودری، مدیرعامل راه‌آهن پرسرعت کالیفرنیا در این هفته، آخرین نشانه‌ای است که نشان می‌دهد این پروژه باید به طور کلی لغو شود. گاوین نیوسام، فرماندار مستقر، زمانی که در سال 2019 به قدرت رسید، متوجه شد.
"این پروژه، همانطور که در حال حاضر برنامه ریزی شده است، هزینه بسیار زیادی خواهد داشت و بسیار طولانی خواهد بود. نظارت بسیار کم و شفافیت کافی وجود ندارد.»
بزرگ‌ترین اخبار، عقاید و فرهنگ‌هایی که در حال حاضر کالیفرنیا را شکل می‌دهند. لطفاً یک ایمیل معتبر ارائه دهید. با کلیک کردن در بالا، با شرایط استفاده و خط‌مشی رازداری موافقت می‌کنید. «در حال حاضر، راهی برای رفتن از ساکرامنتو به سن دیگو وجود ندارد، چه رسد به اینکه از سانفرانسیسکو به لس‌آنجلس. کاش وجود داشت.»
نیوسام درست می گفت. اما او به این ایده پایبند بود که کالیفرنیا می تواند "یک راه آهن پرسرعت بین مرسدس و بیکرزفیلد" ایجاد کند.
هرگز هیچ تقاضای مصرف کننده ای برای پیوند مسافر بین دو شهر روستایی وجود نداشت. پست نیوز کالیفرنیا: فیس بوک، اینستاگرام، تیک تاک، ایکس، یوتیوب، واتس اپ، لینکدین کالیفرنیا پست ورزشی فیس بوک، اینستاگرام، تیک تاک، یوتیوب، ایکس کالیفرنیا پست نظر خبرنامه های کالیفرنیا پست: اینجا ثبت نام کنید! برنامه پست کالیفرنیا: از اینجا دانلود کنید! تحویل در خانه: اینجا ثبت نام کنید! صفحه ششم هالیوود: اینجا ثبت نام کنید! اما پیمانکاران، اتحادیه ها، و سایر منافع خاص باید پرداخت می شدند - از جمله ایالت کالیفرنیا، که می خواست بودجه وزارت حمل و نقل فدرال را حفظ کند.

Lefty firebrand Darializa Avila Chevalier refused to say whether convicted murderers should be put behind bars  — when pressed about her hypocrisy of being a prison abolitionist but also calling for ICE agents to be jailed.

Chevalier, Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s hand-picked Democratic Party candidate for New York’s 13th congressional district, could only offer up a word salad in an interview with Vanity Fair Friday when the reporter repeatedly pushed for the democratic socialist’s answer over what to do with murderers if all jails and prisons were removed.

Mark Guiducci: “Do you believe that someone who is convicted of murder with intent should be physically confined to protect the public?”Darializa Avila Chevalier: “But that is what happens in the day-to-day.”This is Fair Game, where no subject is off the table. Watch the full… pic.twitter.com/PofK1K3IRj

“I’m just curious about now, now that you’re going to become a lawmaker, do you believe that someone who is convicted of murder with intent should be physically confined to protect the public?” the reporter asked.

“But that is what happens in the day-to-day,” Chevalier responded.

“What I argue as someone who deeply cares about ending violence in our communities is that if we don’t begin the process now of building this world where we are proactive in preventing violence instead of reactive, once the violence has already happened, then we’re never going to get to that world.”

The back-and-forth started on the outlet’s podcast when the reporter brought up the calls from Chevalier for police to arrest and lock up the immigration officer who shot an illegal Dominican migrant despite calling for all jails and prisons to be eliminated.

“I see a bit of a contradiction between wanting the shooter apprehended and your stance on prison abolition,” the outlet pressed. “Where is the shooter going if not to jail?”

“You know, abolition is a process and vision, right?” Chevalier said, starting her meandering response. “It is the idea that we are constructing a world where a shooting like that doesn’t happen to begin with.

“And so when I talk about abolishing ICE, the point is that we are taking away the condition for this to ever happen again. We are taking these arms off the street. We are taking these people away from the power to do that to our communities. Right. And we are reinvesting those resources into things that actually make our communities more safe.”

In the days after Oscar Belgal, 28, was shot by an ICE agent in The Bronx earlier this month, Chevalier publicly called for the immigration official to be arrested.

Actor and martial arts fanatic Richard Norton ignored his nurse’s warning about peptide use before his sudden death at age 75.

Norton, who passed away on March 30, 2025, died from “a cardiac arrest at home following self- administration of recently commenced peptide therapy,” according to a newly released coroner’s report obtained by People.

After telling his medical practitioner he was interested in peptide therapy following a previous treatment with another doctor, the Australian actor was approved for the treatment on March 19.

On March 25, he told his doctor that he was feeling good, but just three days later, he “requested a replacement” after allegedly “dropp[ing] and [breaking]” the vial of his treatment.

The high-level athlete was granted the replacement, along with two additional peptides. During that time, he told the nurse that he was taking twice the prescribed dose, while the nurse warned him only to take the prescribed amount.

Per NBC News, he was taking growth hormone peptides CJC1295 and Ipamorelin.

After he had injected the second dose of peptides that evening, his wife, Judy Green, said Norton complained of feeling “hot and flushed and then collapsed and became unresponsive” at around 9 p.m.

She contacted her doctor and medical services, administering CPR until medics arrived before 9:30 p.m.

Clinicians noted that he suffered anaphylaxis followed by cardiac arrest after injecting the peptides.

Peptides, popularized and peddled by RFK Jr. in recent years, have been utilized by many in Hollywood to promote muscle growth, fat loss, skin health and more.

However, many of these peptides — short chains of amino acids — are not FDA-approved, which means much of the market is unregulated.

The coroner believes that this is the first death in Australia linked to peptides.

In a photo taken just a few days before his death, Norton looked fit and healthy as he posed with martial arts instructor Kacey Chong after their session.

The photo was posted on March 19, 2025.

After his death, his wife took to Instagram to share a heartbreaking tribute.

“I am numb and devastated, I have no words I have lost my everything,” she wrote.

“I know there is, and will be lots of love and shock that we have lost this incredible human being. The love ❤️ of my life. I’m using this time to come to terms with my great loss. Judy,” she concluded.

news.originalContent:
The 9th Circuit Court called the petition to remove 20,000 ballots from California’s vote count unconstitutional.

For the second time in less than a week, an appeals court in the United States has rejected a petition from the administration of President Donald Trump to set aside 20,000 ballots in California over concerns about non-citizen voting.

The decision arrived on Friday, with less than four days to go until the November 3 midterm elections.

The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Trump’s request would not only violate the US Constitution but also risk disenfranchising eligible voters.

“The consequence of the United States’s request is not merely ballot segregation, but ultimately both the cancellation of the ballot and the removal of voters from the voting rolls,” the majority wrote in its ruling.

Two judges — Mark Bennett and Gabriel Sanchez — formed the majority. They were appointed by Trump and his Democratic predecessor Joe Biden, respectively.

A third judge, Trump appointee Patrick Bumatay, issued a dissent, calling the administration’s petition a “reasonable request”.

The Trump administration has claimed that nearly 20,000 “likely non-citizens” received mail-in ballots to vote in California’s midterm elections on November 3. It sued the state on October 15 to prevent those ballots from being counted.

But the accuracy of the Trump administration’s list has been called into doubt, as have its claims of widespread non-citizen voting.

Election fraud in the US is extremely rare. So is non-citizen voting, despite Trump’s assertion earlier this year that as many as 278,000 foreign nationals across the country were registered to cast a ballot.

Like California, states like Nevada and Washington have also received lists of alleged non-citizen voters, but officials there have found the documents to be largely inaccurate.

In Nevada, for instance, state authorities ultimately issued a statement in September saying that the Trump administration had erroneously identified citizens as non-citizens on its list. Not a single name was correct, according to the statement.

California is a Democratic stronghold, and on November 3, it will elect 52 members of the House of Representatives, one of Congress’s two chambers.

The state, however, has long been a target for criticism under Trump, who has accused its Democratic leadership of “cheating” in elections.

But California officials, including Governor Gavin Newsom, have countered that the Trump administration is seeking to meddle in the state’s elections to sow voter distrust and undermine the election results.

“This is a sad, desperate attempt by Trump to use his politicized Justice Department to try to suppress California voters,” Newsom said in a news release, following the October 15 lawsuit.

Non-citizen voting in federal elections is against the law in all 50 US states, including California.

The Constitution’s Election Clause also grants states the exclusive authority to administer elections, though it does allow for Congress to pass regulations concerning voting procedures.

The Trump administration initially sent California its list of 20,000 “likely non-citizens” on October 12, barely three weeks before the midterm election.

But California officials refused its demand to set aside the 20,000 ballots, requesting instead proof that the names on the list were indeed foreign nationals. According to the California government, no such evidence has been provided.

The Trump administration last week charged 28 foreign nationals in California with election-related infractions, but some of the accused told the Los Angeles Times they had never registered to vote.

The newspaper’s reporting suggested some of the non-citizen defendants shared the same name as eligible voters.

As the October 15 lawsuit navigated the court system earlier this month, the Trump administration sought an emergency ruling from the 9th Circuit Court to suspend the 20,000 ballots.

But the appeals court rejected that petition on Monday, saying that the Trump administration had not given lower courts adequate time to weigh the matter.

A lower court ultimately ruled against the Trump administration on Wednesday, and it again appealed to the 9th Circuit Court.

In its majority decision, the appeals court framed the Trump administration’s lawsuit as an attempt to violate the Constitution’s Election Clause.

“We decline the United States’s invitation to contravene the Elections Clause by undermining the Constitution’s plain text,” the majority wrote.

The majority also wrote that it had “major concerns” that granting the Trump administration’s request would “harm the public interest by risking the disenfranchisement of eligible voters and putting the entire tabulation process in jeopardy”.

news.originalContent:
The United States has scrapped a traditional group photo of foreign ministers after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.

The move exposes deep rifts at the heart of the Group of 20 (G20), whose foreign ministers are meeting in the southern city of Atlanta in the United States for talks overshadowed by the wars in Ukraine and Iran.

“There will be no family photo featuring our European partners together with Mr Lavrov,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said, according to the dpa news agency.

Lavrov, who remains under Western sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, arrived in Atlanta ahead of the talks, Russian state media reported. Moscow said on Thursday that he would use his speech to argue against international sanctions. Ukraine was not invited, the Abu Dhabi-based newspaper The National reported.

A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Russia’s presence at the G20 “in no way legitimises its actions”.

The European Union’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas pledged on Thursday to urge G20 partners to strengthen support for Ukraine and pursue accountability through a special tribunal and claims commission, after a Russian strike on a Ukrainian railway station killed at least 14 people earlier that day.

The meeting also comes weeks after US President Donald Trump issued sanctions waivers allowing Russia to export diesel to ease fuel prices before the November 3 midterm elections.

Opening the talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged members to cooperate on economic and geopolitical crises threatening global trade, energy and food supplies, and freedom of navigation, dpa reported. Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz after US-Israeli strikes began in late February, and global energy prices have risen sharply since.

“Both maritime and food security drive economic security,” Rubio wrote on X.

No joint statement is expected. A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Washington will instead publish a chair’s summary it has drafted. The source added: “The G20 is no longer really a forum where foreign ministers can reach agreement on a statement.”

No government has said whether Rubio and Lavrov will hold a formal bilateral meeting.

China sent Executive Vice Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu in place of Foreign Minister Wang Yi, according to a delegation list released by the Department of State. South Africa, a founding G20 member, has been excluded by Washington, and the African Union is represented by Burundi’s Edouard Bizimana.

The Atlanta talks are the last ministerial meeting of the US G20 presidency before leaders meet in Miami on December 14 and 15.
news.content: پس از اینکه مقامات اروپایی حاضر نشدند در کنار سرگئی لاوروف وزیر امور خارجه روسیه قرار بگیرند، ایالات متحده عکس گروهی سنتی از وزرای خارجه را حذف کرد. این اقدام شکاف‌های عمیقی را در قلب گروه 20 (G20) آشکار می‌کند، که وزرای خارجه آن در شهر جنوبی آتلانتا در ایالات متحده برای گفتگوهایی که تحت الشعاع جنگ‌های اوکراین و ایران قرار گرفته است، گرد هم می‌آیند. به گزارش خبرگزاری dpa، یوهان وادفول، وزیر امور خارجه آلمان گفت: «هیچ عکس خانوادگی که شرکای اروپایی ما را به همراه آقای لاوروف نشان دهد، وجود نخواهد داشت.» رسانه دولتی روسیه گزارش داد، لاوروف که همچنان تحت تحریم های غرب اعمال شده پس از تهاجم کامل روسیه به اوکراین در سال 2022 قرار دارد، قبل از مذاکرات وارد آتلانتا شد. مسکو روز پنجشنبه گفت که از سخنرانی خود برای استدلال علیه تحریم های بین المللی استفاده خواهد کرد. روزنامه نشنال چاپ ابوظبی گزارش داد که اوکراین دعوت نشده است. یک منبع دیپلماتیک به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت که حضور روسیه در G20 "به هیچ وجه به اقدامات این کشور مشروعیت نمی بخشد". پس از حمله روسیه به ایستگاه راه آهن اوکراین در اوایل همان روز، کاجا کالاس، مسئول سیاست خارجی اتحادیه اروپا، روز پنجشنبه متعهد شد که از شرکای گروه 20 بخواهد حمایت از اوکراین را تقویت کنند و از طریق یک دادگاه ویژه و کمیسیون ادعایی پاسخگویی را پیگیری کنند. این نشست همچنین هفته‌ها پس از آن برگزار می‌شود که دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا معافیت‌هایی از تحریم‌ها را صادر کرد که به روسیه اجازه می‌داد تا پیش از انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای 3 نوامبر برای کاهش قیمت سوخت، گازوئیل صادر کند.

news.originalContent:
Despite efforts to restore damaged infrastructure, residents face soaring water costs as war, displacement strain supplies.

Port Sudan, Sudan – Every day, Amina Khalafallah spends 10,000 Sudanese pounds ($1 at the parallel market rate) on water for herself and her four children. Over a 30-day month, that amounts to 300,000 pounds ($30) – the equivalent of her entire monthly salary.

Khalafallah lives in the Deim Mayo neighbourhood of Port Sudan, in eastern Sudan, where her home is not connected to a piped water network. Instead, she depends on street vendors, who charge 1,000 pounds ($0.10) for 18 litres.

Khalafallah works in a cafeteria at a private institution, while her husband works in another state and sends money to help her out when he can.

Between them, the family barely scrambles enough money to get by, but Khalafallah says she often has to borrow money. It’s a typical story in Sudan, where, according to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the country’s more than three-year-long war has pushed average incomes back to levels last seen in the early 1990s.

The hotter months bring additional challenges, as water prices rise and vendors become harder to find.

“We make sure to set aside money for water in the summer before covering our other household needs, even if that means going without some essentials,” Khalafallah told Al Jazeera.

According to the African Development Bank (AfDB), access to safe water is one of Sudan’s most urgent needs, with millions of children at risk of waterborne diseases.

In Port Sudan, relatively safe from the fighting that has plagued other areas of the country, the arrival of people displaced by the war has put additional pressure on already fragile infrastructure. The AfDB has reported that the city’s water supply was meeting less than 40 percent of demand.

One of the major issues Port Sudan has faced is the collapse of the Arbaat Dam. Located in the Red Sea Hills northwest of Port Sudan, it once supplied half of the coastal city’s daily water needs.

But in August 2024, heavy rainfall and flooding caused the dam to collapse, destroying villages downstream and damaging pipelines and wells.

As a result of the collapse, entire neighbourhoods are dependent on expensive water deliveries by truck.

Ahmed Osman, 30, has spent the past three years working at a water distribution station that supplies street vendors who deliver water to households.

When Sudan’s war began in April 2023, Osman said he charged vendors 4,000 Sudanese pounds ($0.40) to fill a donkey-drawn cart carrying at least 250 litres of water.

Those prices have since risen sharply, he said, because of increasing operating costs, particularly the fuel needed to transport water to his distribution station.

“A water tanker carrying 50,000 litres of water now costs 1.5 million Sudanese pounds [$150], compared with about 450,000 pounds before the war,” Osman told Al Jazeera.

Osman keeps the water in storage tanks before pumping it into the vendors’ carts. He charges 16,000 pounds ($1.60) to fill a cart carrying 250 litres.

After his expenses, Osman typically makes a profit of about 70,000 pounds ($7) per day, split between him and his partner.

Rehabilitation work has restored parts of the damaged water network.

According to the UNDP, the restoration work has included drilling or rehabilitating 15 boreholes, laying 17 kilometres (10.5 miles) of new pipelines, as well as installing solar-powered pumps.

The UNDP said the restored system could supply water to nearly 230,000 people.

However, that would still not be enough to supply water to all of Port Sudan, which the UNDP estimates to now have a population of one million people.

Other projects are therefore necessary to meet the water needs of residents – including one launched in June by the AfDB and UNICEF, which intends to expand access to safe water for up to 750,000 people in the city.

Emad Hafez, medical director of the emergency department at Port Sudan Teaching Hospital, told Al Jazeera the water crisis poses serious risks to public health, increasing the risk of waterborne diseases and making it harder for families to maintain basic hygiene.

He warned that disruptions to water supplies can force families to rely on untreated water, increasing the risk of cholera and other diarrhoeal diseases, particularly during the rainy season and in overcrowded displacement camps.

“Water shortages can also make it harder for families to maintain adequate hygiene, increasing the risk of skin infections and other hygiene-related illnesses,” Hafez said. “Meanwhile, storing water in uncovered containers can create breeding sites for mosquitoes, raising the risk of vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue fever.”

Water shortages also threaten healthcare services, Hafez said, explaining that hospitals require reliable supplies for infection prevention, cleaning and patient care.

“Beyond its immediate health consequences, water insecurity can worsen food shortages and malnutrition by disrupting agricultural activities and placing additional financial pressure on already vulnerable households,” he said. “Children under five and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable to the effects of inadequate nutrition.”
news.content: علیرغم تلاش‌ها برای بازسازی زیرساخت‌های آسیب‌دیده، ساکنان با هزینه‌های سرسام‌آور آب به دلیل جنگ، منابع آوارگان مواجه هستند. بندر سودان، سودان - آمنه خلف الله هر روز 10000 پوند سودانی (1 دلار به نرخ بازار موازی) برای آب خود و چهار فرزندش خرج می‌کند. در طول یک ماه 30 روزه، این مبلغ به 300000 پوند (30 دلار) می رسد - معادل کل حقوق ماهانه او. خلف الله در محله دیم مایو پورت سودان در شرق سودان زندگی می کند، جایی که خانه اش به شبکه آب لوله کشی متصل نیست. در عوض، او به فروشندگان خیابانی وابسته است، که برای 18 لیتر 1000 پوند (0.10 دلار) می گیرند. خلف الله در یک کافه تریا در یک موسسه خصوصی کار می کند، در حالی که شوهرش در ایالت دیگر کار می کند و در صورت امکان برای کمک به او پول می فرستد. بین آنها، خانواده به سختی پول کافی برای گذراندن زندگی خود را به دست می آورند، اما خلف الله می گوید که او اغلب مجبور است پول قرض کند. این یک داستان معمولی در سودان است، جایی که طبق برنامه توسعه سازمان ملل متحد (UNDP)، ​​جنگ بیش از سه ساله این کشور میانگین درآمد را به سطحی که آخرین بار در اوایل دهه 1990 مشاهده شده بود، رسانده است. ماه‌های گرمتر چالش‌های بیشتری را به همراه دارد، زیرا قیمت آب افزایش می‌یابد و یافتن فروشندگان سخت‌تر می‌شود. خلف الله به الجزیره گفت: «ما مطمئن می شویم که قبل از تأمین سایر نیازهای خانوار خود، در تابستان قبل از تأمین نیازهای خانگی خود، پولی را برای آب کنار می گذاریم، حتی اگر این به معنای رفتن بدون نیازهای ضروری باشد.» بر اساس گزارش بانک توسعه آفریقا (AfDB)، دسترسی به آب سالم یکی از ضروری ترین نیازهای سودان است، با میلیون ها نفر.

Both sides signed a digital trade deal, as Trump’s trade threats push Washington’s allies to seek closer ties elsewhere.

The European Union and Canada have launched what they described as an Alliance for the Future, as Ottawa prepares to become the bloc’s first so-called “associate member”.

Prime Minister Mark Carney hosted the Canada-EU summit in Montreal and signed a digital trade deal, alongside other agreements. Also at the Friday summit were European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa.

The term “associate member” has no legal basis and is contested by some EU states. However, its use underscores the desire of Canada and the EU to forge closer relations, as United States President Donald Trump continues to threaten Washington’s traditional allies with trade tariffs if they do not play by his rules.

“Canada and the EU are working to establish the closest possible partnership, which will be far from full membership, but which will make Canada the first associate member of the European Union,” Carney posted on X.

“Today in Montreal, we have taken a major step forward by establishing more than twenty measures that will increase affordability, create opportunities and ensure our sovereignty on both sides of the Atlantic.”

In a joint statement following the summit, the two sides announced an agreement under which the European Investment Bank will invest in critical Canadian resources, particularly raw minerals. They also said they would advance cooperation on artificial intelligence security and safety.

“A more dangerous and divided world has fundamentally changed the requirements of sovereignty. It is no longer enough for nations to feed, fuel and defend ourselves,” the statement said.

It added that “true sovereignty” requires secure access to critical minerals, semiconductors, payment systems, energy, vaccines, space-based communications and AI.

Ukraine was also on the meeting agenda, with Carney announcing Canada’s participation in the EU’s 90 billion euro ($103bn) support loan for Kyiv. Carney said Canada would make an initial contribution of 500 million euros ($558m).

Opportunities for students in Canada and the EU were also discussed. Both sides said they would launch negotiations aimed at deepening Ottawa’s participation in Erasmus+, the EU’s flagship student exchange programme.

Carney and Trump are currently engaged in a trade dispute, with talks under way to reach a deal between the two countries.
news.content: هر دو طرف یک قرارداد تجارت دیجیتال را امضا کردند، زیرا تهدیدات تجاری ترامپ، متحدان واشنگتن را وادار می کند تا به دنبال روابط نزدیک تر در جاهای دیگر باشند. اتحادیه اروپا و کانادا آنچه را که به عنوان اتحاد برای آینده توصیف می کنند، راه اندازی کرده اند، زیرا اتاوا در حال آماده شدن برای تبدیل شدن به اولین به اصطلاح "عضو وابسته" بلوک است. توافق نامه ها همچنین در اجلاس روز جمعه، اورسولا فون در لاین، رئیس کمیسیون اروپا و آنتونیو کاستا، رئیس شورای اروپا حضور داشتند. اصطلاح "عضو وابسته" هیچ مبنای قانونی ندارد و توسط برخی از کشورهای اتحادیه اروپا مورد اعتراض است. با این حال، استفاده از آن بر تمایل کانادا و اتحادیه اروپا برای ایجاد روابط نزدیک‌تر تأکید می‌کند، زیرا دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور ایالات متحده همچنان متحدان سنتی واشنگتن را تهدید می‌کند که در صورت عدم اجرای قوانین او، تعرفه‌های تجاری اعمال خواهند کرد. کارنی در پستی در X نوشت: «کانادا و اتحادیه اروپا در حال کار برای ایجاد نزدیک‌ترین مشارکت ممکن هستند، که با عضویت کامل فاصله زیادی دارد، اما کانادا را به اولین عضو وابسته اتحادیه اروپا تبدیل می‌کند.» امروز در مونترال، ما با ایجاد بیش از بیست اقدام که مقرون به صرفه بودن، ایجاد فرصت‌ها و تضمین حق حاکمیت ما در آتلانتیک را در هر دو طرف تضمین می‌کند، گام بزرگی به جلو برداشته‌ایم. در بیانیه ای مشترک پس از این اجلاس، دو طرف توافقی را اعلام کردند که بر اساس آن بانک سرمایه گذاری اروپا در منابع مهم کانادا، به ویژه مواد معدنی خام سرمایه گذاری خواهد کرد. آنها نیز

news.originalContent:
Redistricting in California, the most populous US state, could flip control of US House from Republican to Democrat.

As voters across the United States head to the polls for the midterm elections – widely seen as a referendum on President Donald Trump’s second term in office – the state of California is set to play an important role.

Several races across the country’s most populous state could help determine whether the Democratic Party takes control of the US House of Representatives, where Trump’s Republican Party currently holds a slim majority.

California’s ballot initiatives – or policy decisions made by voters – have also received national attention.

Perhaps the biggest difference in this year’s elections, however, is the introduction of new congressional district maps drawn up through a partisan redistricting initiative approved by California voters last year.

That initiative aims to net at least five additional Democratic Party seats in the House, where Republicans have a four-seat majority.

Which California races are competitive, who are the main candidates and how has the state’s redistricting push changed the electoral landscape?

The election will be held on Tuesday, November 3. California polls will be open from 7am (15:00 GMT) to 8pm (04:00 GMT Wednesday). Mail ballots must be postmarked by election day.

The House is divided into 435 districts, each represented by one member of Congress elected by their constituents. While congressional districts are populated equally, their boundaries are set by states and can shift.

Partisan redistricting involves states drawing those district maps in a way that advantages candidates from one party over another.

California Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat and Trump critic, first proposed a one-time statewide redistricting effort in response to seven Republican-led states redrawing their maps in an attempt to secure seats for Republicans. Although California had banned partisan redistricting, Newsom pitched the idea as an unfortunate but necessary retaliatory measure.

California voters approved the redistricting plan in a 2025 ballot measure – Proposition 50 – that temporarily suspended the state’s nonpartisan redistricting commission until 2030. California then drew new maps to make several Republican strongholds more competitive for Democratic challengers.

As a result, the handful of districts previously seen as favourable terrain for Republicans have instead become hotly-contested races between the two parties.

California has 52 members in the House of Representatives – the most of any state – with Republicans holding just eight of the seats. There are several closely watched state races in the Democratic Party’s effort to secure a majority in the House, the lower chamber of the US Congress.

One is the 22nd congressional district, located in California’s agriculture-rich Central Valley. The district map was redrawn under Proposition 50, setting up one of the state’s most contentious races in a former Republican stronghold.

Incumbent Republican Representative David Valadao is locked in a tight race with Democratic challenger Randy Villegas. Valadao has portrayed himself as a moderate, while Villegas has hammered him over issues such as the rising cost of living, healthcare and Trump’s immigration crackdowns – a key issue for the area’s immigrant farm-working communities.

California’s 48th district, a traditionally Republican stronghold which includes parts of San Diego County near the border with Mexico, is also considered highly competitive after its boundaries were redrawn. The district’s longtime representative, Republican Darrell Issa, decided to retire after the redistricting, with two local officials – Republican Jim Desmond and Democratic San Diego Councilmember Marni von Wilpert – now vying for the seat.

While California’s redistricting aimed to make historically reliable Republican districts more competitive for Democrats, the process has also had some unexpected impacts: Two Republican members of Congress, Representatives Ken Calvert and Young Kim, have found themselves locked in a bitter race against each other after redrawn maps put them in the same district.

Vying to replace Governor Newsom are Republican political commentator Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra. Becerra is a former California attorney general and secretary of health and human services during former President Joe Biden’s administration.

Hilton has blasted Becerra for rising crime and homelessness as well as high fuel prices in California, where a gallon (3.78 litres) of petrol costs $5.95 compared with $4.22 nationally, according to the American Automobile Association. Heavily favoured in the Democratic stronghold state, Becerra has sought to associate Hilton with Trump, who is deeply unpopular among Californians.

Polls show Becerra with a strong lead over the Republican challenger. A recent Emerson poll suggested that he was ahead by 27 points.

California voters will also weigh in on a handful of policy questions, including a tax on billionaires and whether the state should adopt mandatory voter ID.

Perhaps the most contentious is Proposition 40, a one-time tax on billionaires to help fund healthcare and education. The measure is one of three impacting the state’s ultra-wealthy residents, with the referendums dubbed the “billionaire battle”.

The tax would apply to about 200 of the wealthiest people in California, according to the news website CalMatters. The proposition is opposed by powerful industries and tech titans, who have poured more than $152m into fighting the ballot measure compared with $33m raised in support of the tax, a California public radio station KQED reports.

The measure has drawn opposition from figures such as Google cofounder Sergey Brin, who has given more than $102m to defeat the referendum, as well as Hilton, Becerra and Newsom. Despite being supported by the Democratic Party, Proposition 40 is also being fought by some progressive groups opposed to the one-time tax.

Other progressives such as Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Ro Khanna, a wealthy member of Congress from California’s Silicon Valley, support the referendum.

Two other ballot measures, Propositions 41 and 42, would effectively nullify Proposition 40 if approved by voters.

Another measure, Proposition 39, has also been the subject of fierce debate. If passed, it would require Californians to show government-issued IDs in order to vote.

While supporters say mandatory IDs will bolster confidence in elections by countering voter fraud, studies have found that fraudulent voting is nearly nonexistent in the US.

Critics say that voter ID laws add obstacles to voting by requiring government-issued documents, such as a driver’s licence, that not all citizens hold. They argue that strong safeguards ensuring only eligible voters cast ballots are already in place.
news.content: تغییر منطقه در کالیفرنیا، پرجمعیت‌ترین ایالت آمریکا، می‌تواند کنترل مجلس نمایندگان آمریکا را از جمهوری‌خواه به دموکرات تبدیل کند. در حالی که رای‌دهندگان در سراسر ایالات متحده برای انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای به پای صندوق‌های رای می‌روند - که به طور گسترده به عنوان یک همه‌پرسی برای دومین دوره ریاست جمهوری دونالد ترامپ دیده می‌شود - ایالت کالیفرنیا نقش مهمی ایفا خواهد کرد. چندین رقابت در پرجمعیت‌ترین ایالت این کشور می‌تواند به تعیین اینکه آیا حزب دموکرات کنترل مجلس نمایندگان ایالات متحده را در دست می‌گیرد، جایی که حزب جمهوری‌خواه ترامپ در حال حاضر اکثریت کمی را در اختیار دارد، کمک کند. با این حال، شاید بزرگ‌ترین تفاوت در انتخابات امسال، معرفی نقشه‌های نواحی جدید کنگره باشد که از طریق یک طرح تقسیم بندی مجدد حزبی که توسط رأی‌دهندگان کالیفرنیا در سال گذشته تصویب شد، تهیه شده است. هدف این ابتکار کسب حداقل پنج کرسی اضافی از حزب دموکرات در مجلس است، جایی که جمهوری‌خواهان دارای اکثریت چهار کرسی هستند. کدامیک از رقابت‌های کالیفرنیا رقابتی هستند، نامزدهای اصلی چه کسانی هستند و چگونه فشار منطقه‌ای مجدد این ایالت چشم‌انداز انتخاباتی را تغییر داده است؟ انتخابات در روز سه‌شنبه، 3 نوامبر برگزار می‌شود. صندوق‌های رای در کالیفرنیا از ساعت 7 صبح (15:00 به وقت گرینویچ) تا 8 بعد از ظهر (04:00 به وقت گرینویچ چهارشنبه) باز خواهند بود. برگه های رای نامه پستی باید تا روز انتخابات مهر پست شوند. مجلس نمایندگان به 435 ناحیه تقسیم شده است که هر یک توسط یک عضو کنگره که توسط رای دهندگان آنها انتخاب می شود، نمایندگی می شود. در حالی که مناطق کنگره مردمی هستند

news.originalContent:
Prime Minister claims the parties accepted foreign funding.

The votes have been counted in Israel’s general election and there is no overall majority.

Benjamin Netanyahu has accused Palestinian Israeli parties of “stealing” the polls and accepting funding from Qatar to do it.

Those parties have denied wrongdoing, the Electoral Commission has found no evidence of fraud and Qatar denies any involvement.

So, is this a way for Netanyahu to stop Palestinian Israeli parties from forming a coalition with the opposition to unseat his Likud party?

Presenter: Mohammed Jamjoom

Sheikha Alanoud Hamad Saud Al Thani – political analyst and fellow at the Middle East Council on Global Affairs

Abed Abou Shhadeh – political analyst and former City Council Representative for the Palestinian community in Jaffa-Tel Aviv

Adam Bellos – CEO of The Israel Innovation Fund and columnist for The Jerusalem Post

ایران از سوی کشورها
news.originalContent:
محمدجواد حاج‌علی‌اکبری، امام جمعه موقت تهران، خواستار بازنگری در دکترین هسته‌ای جمهوری اسلامی ایران است.

در ادبیات سیاسی و موضوعات مرتبط با اشاعه تسلیحات هسته‌ای، بازنگری در دکترین هسته‌ای می‌تواند به معنای تغییر سیاست درباره دستیابی به سلاح اتمی باشد.

آقای حاج‌علی‌اکبری امروز، هشتم آبان/۳۰ اکتبر، در خطبه‌های نماز جمعه تهران گفت که این موضوع به یک «مطالبه ملی» تبدیل شده است.

ایران از سوی کشورهای غربی با اتهام تلاش برای دستیابی به تسلیحات هسته‌ای در پوشش یک برنامه صلح‌آمیز روبه‌روست، اما همواره این اتهام را رد کرده و می‌گوید که برنامه هسته‌ای آن فقط اهداف صلح‌آمیز دارد.

امام جمعه موقت تهران در اظهاراتی متفاوت از گذشته گفت: «این موضوع واکنشی شتاب‌زده و هیجانی نیست، بلکه برآمده از آگاهی و تجربه تاریخی ملت ایران در مواجهه با بدعهدی‌های آمریکاست و ریشه در حق ملت برای برخورداری از امنیت و زندگی عزتمندانه دارد.»

آقای حاج‌علی‌اکبری می‌گوید که بر اساس برخی نظرسنجی‌های پیشین، بیش از «۷۰ درصد مردم از تغییر دکترین هسته‌ای حمایت می‌کنند»، اما به منبع این نظرسنجی‌ها اشاره نکرد.

او از کارشناسان خواست پیشنهادهای خود را با همکاری نهادهای مسئول تهیه و برای تصمیم‌گیری نهایی به مجتبی خامنه‌ای ارائه کنند.

امام جمعه موقت تهران گفت: «چرا نباید در دکترین هسته‌ای تجدیدنظر کنیم؟ ملت ایران در طول سال‌های گذشته تجربه‌های دردناکی از رفتار آمریکا داشته است؛ طرف مقابل از خطوط قرمز ملت ایران عبور کرده» و «به تعهدات و توافق‌های خود پایبند نمانده است.»

او افزود: «ملت ایران در مسیرهای مختلف فرصت تعامل و توافق را فراهم کرده، اما تجربه بدعهدی‌های طرف مقابل، ضرورت بازنگری در برخی محاسبات امنیتی را به یک موضوع جدی تبدیل کرده است.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

پیش از این نیز اظهاراتی از مقام‌ها و چهره‌هایی در ایران درباره توانایی ساخت سلاح هسته‌ای یا ابعاد نظامی برنامه هسته‌ای این کشور منتشر شده بود، اما به نظر می‌رسد طرح «ضرورت بازنگری در دکترین هسته‌ای ایران» در نماز جمعه تهران، این موضوع را به بحثی عمومی‌تر تبدیل می‌کند.

پیش‌تر کمال خرازی، رئیس شورای راهبردی روابط خارجی ایران که در حمله اسرائیل کشته شد، و محمد اسلامی، رئیس سازمان انرژی اتمی ایران، از توانایی این کشور برای ساخت سلاح اتمی سخن گفته بودند، اما تأکید داشتند که با وجود این توانایی، جمهوری اسلامی ایران قصدی برای ساخت آن ندارد.

علی‌اکبر صالحی، وزیر خارجه پیشین و رئیس اسبق سازمان انرژی اتمی ایران، هم قبلاً گفته بود که تجدیدنظر در سیاست هسته‌ای جزو اختیارات علی خامنه‌ای است. آقای خامنه‌ای روز نهم اسفند، در ساعات نخست حملات اسرائیل و آمریکا به ایران، کشته شد.

علی خامنه‌ای در یک سخنرانی گفته بود که تولید، نگهداری و استفاده از سلاح اتمی را حرام می‌داند.

مقام‌های دولتی پس از این اظهارات، آن را با عنوان «فتوای اتمی» به‌عنوان سند به سازمان ملل متحد ارائه کردند و هر بار که پرونده اتمی ایران وضعیت بحرانی‌تری پیدا می‌کرد، با استناد به آن اعلام می‌کردند که جمهوری اسلامی از ساخت هرگونه سلاح اتمی خودداری خواهد کرد و از نظر مذهبی نیز آن را حرام می‌داند.

مجتبی خامنه‌ای که پس از کشته‌شدن پدرش به جانشینی او انتخاب شد، تاکنون موضع صریحی در این باره نگرفته است. او تاکنون در انظار عمومی ظاهر نشده و فیلم یا فایل صوتی از او پس از رسیدن به جانشینی پدرش منتشر نشده است.

رسانه‌های بین‌المللی غیبت آقای علی‌اف را نشانه‌ای دیگر از تیرگی روابط ترکیه و جمهوری آذربایجان دانستند.

در هفته‌های اخیر، انتقاد مقام‌ها و چهره‌های سیاسی ترکیه از مقررات جدید حجاب در آذربایجان به اختلافات دو کشور دامن زده است. آذربایجان مقررات جدیدی برای پوشش دانش‌آموزان و معلمان وضع کرده که اگرچه به‌صراحت حجاب را ممنوع نکرده، اما گزارش‌هایی از جلوگیری از ورود دختران محجبه به مدارس و محدودیت فعالیت معلمان محجبه منتشر شده است.

آذربایجان می‌گوید که این مقررات بر مبنای اصول سکولار تنظیم شده است.

رجب طیب اردوغان، رئیس‌جمهور ترکیه، روز جمعه در نشست آنکارا، بدون نام بردن از جمهوری آذربایجان گفت: «در تصویر خانواده ما جایی برای جدایی، تفرقه یا درگیری نیست. همه ما یکی هستیم و در کنار هم قرار داریم و به خواست خدا، تا ابد برادر خواهیم ماند.»

جیحون بایراموف، وزیر خارجه جمهوری آذربایجان، نمایندگی این کشور در نشست سران کشورهای ترک را بر عهده داشت. او پس از سخنرانی آقای اردوغان، بدون اشاره به تنش‌های اخیر، از ترکیه به خاطر میزبانی نشست تشکر کرد.

چنین سطحی از تنش در روابط ترکیه و جمهوری آذربایجان کم‌سابقه است.

ترکیه و جمهوری آذربایجان همواره روابط خود را با عبارت «دو کشور، یک ملت» توصیف کرده‌اند.

تیرگی روابط دو کشور در حالی است که پس از حمایت ترکیه از جمهوری آذربایجان در جنگ قره‌باغ کوهستانی در سال ۲۰۲۳، همکاری‌های دو کشور به سطح بی‌سابقه‌ای رسیده بود.

ترکیه از خریداران اصلی گاز طبیعی جمهوری آذربایجان است.

آقای اردوغان در همین هفته یکی از مشاورانش را پس از انتقاد علنی او از تصمیم جمهوری آذربایجان درباره حجاب در مدارس برکنار کرده بود.

دفتر ریاست‌جمهوری ترکیه اعلام کرد که آقای اردوغان هفته گذشته نیز در جریان یک تماس تلفنی، شخصاً از الهام علی‌اف دعوت کرده بود تا در نشست سازمان کشورهای ترک شرکت کند.

خبرگزاری آذری‌پرس، بدون اشاره به منبع خبر، گزارش داد که آقای علی‌اف به دلیل «برنامه‌های از پیش تعیین‌شده و فشردگی برنامه کاری» در این نشست شرکت نکرده است. از جمله این برنامه‌ها، مراسم و جشنواره‌ای در چارچوب جام جهانی زیر ۱۵ سال فیفا در باکو عنوان شده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

مقام‌های جمهوری آذربایجان تاکنون درباره علت غیبت آقای علی‌اف در نشست اظهارنظر رسمی نکرده‌اند.

در همین حال، ترکیه می‌کوشد روابط خود را با ارمنستان عادی کند و مرز مشترکش را به روی این کشور بازگشایی کند؛ هرچند آنکارا این موضوع را به پیشرفت روند صلح میان جمهوری آذربایجان و ارمنستان مشروط کرده است.

اما جدای از عادی‌سازی روابط با ارمنستان، اختلاف بر سر اسرائیل و فلسطین از مسائل حساس‌تر میان دو کشور تلقی می‌شود.

ترکیه پس از حملات حماس در هفتم اکتبر ۲۰۲۳ و آغاز عملیات نظامی گسترده اسرائیل در غزه، به یکی از کشورهایی تبدیل شد که تندترین مواضع را علیه اسرائیل اتخاذ کردند.

در مقابل، جمهوری آذربایجان برای روابط خود با اسرائیل، به‌ویژه در حوزه‌های امنیتی، اطلاعاتی و انرژی، اهمیت راهبردی قائل است. باکو مقادیر قابل توجهی سلاح از اسرائیل خریداری می‌کند و در مقابل، بخش بزرگی از نیازهای نفتی این کشور را تأمین می‌کند.

اخیراً در ادامه هشدارهای غیرمستقیم به ترکیه، وزارت خارجه جمهوری آذربایجان در ماه جاری میلادی ۳۱ شهروند ترکیه را به دلیل مطالب منتشرشده در شبکه‌های اجتماعی که آنها را علیه حاکمیت و امنیت جمهوری آذربایجان دانسته، «عناصر نامطلوب» اعلام و ورودشان را به این کشور ممنوع کرده است.

هاکان فیدان، وزیر خارجه ترکیه، نیز در همین ماه پس از دیدار با علی‌اف در نشستی در باکو گفت که در شبکه‌های اجتماعی اطلاعات نادرستی درباره روابط ترکیه و جمهوری آذربایجان منتشر می‌شود. او در عین حال تأکید کرد که دو کشور می‌توانند اختلافات خود را از طریق گفت‌وگو حل‌وفصل کنند.

البته شرکت نکردن رهبران دو کشور در چنین نشست‌هایی بی‌سابقه نیست. دو سال پیش، زمانی که آقای اردوغان در نشست غیررسمی سران کشورهای ترک در شوشا شرکت نکرد، شماری از ناظران درباره سرد شدن روابط دو کشور هشدار داده بودند.

مایکروسافت به دنبال کسب حداقل 25 میلیارد دلار در اولین فروش اوراق قرضه خود در ایالات متحده در بیش از 9 سال در روز پنجشنبه بود، زیرا این غول فناوری به دنبال توسعه گسترده هوش مصنوعی است که انتظار می رود هزینه سرمایه خود را در سال 2026 به حد
news.originalContent:
(Photo by NOEL CELIS/AFP via Getty Images)

Microsoft was seeking to raise at least $25 billion in its first U.S. bond sale in more than nine years Thursday as the technology giant pursues a massive artificial intelligence expansion expected to push its capital spending to approximately $170 billion in 2026.

The planned borrowing marks Microsoft’s return to the American investment-grade bond market for the first time since 2017, underscoring the costs associated with building the infrastructure powering the AI boom. The offering follows the company’s disclosure Wednesday that it expects to spend more than $50 billion on capital expenditures during the current quarter alone, raising questions about how even the nation’s most profitable technology companies will finance their growing AI ambitions. (RELATED: Microsoft Offers Buyouts To 60,000 Employees As AI Spending Soars)

Microsoft is marketing the bonds across ten tranches with maturities ranging from two to 40 years, according to Bloomberg. The company last tapped the U.S. investment-grade bond market in 2017, when it raised $17 billion.

The proceeds are expected to support general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures, working capital, acquisitions, share repurchases and the repayment of existing debt. Microsoft has not indicated that the entire offering will be dedicated to AI investments.

The borrowing follows Microsoft’s fiscal first-quarter earnings call Wednesday, when Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood outlined the company’s infrastructure spending requirements and acknowledged that additional financing could supplement the cash generated by its operations.

“To complement cash generated by the business and preserve financial flexibility, we will access additional sources of funding when we believe it is attractive to do so,” Hood said during the call.

Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures during the three months ending Sept. 30, with approximately three-quarters of that spending directed toward shorter-lived assets, primarily central processing units and graphics processing units used in data centers.

The spending figures illustrate the financial demands of competing in the AI industry, where technology companies are committing billions to specialized computer chips, electricity-intensive data centers and the infrastructure required to train and operate increasingly sophisticated AI models.

Hood said the company expects capital expenditures to exceed $50 billion during the quarter ending in December, bringing its projected calendar-year spending to approximately $170 billion. She also indicated that spending would accelerate during the second half of Microsoft’s fiscal year as delayed infrastructure capacity becomes available and the company continues purchasing processors, memory and storage equipment.

The $170 billion projection represents a reduction from Microsoft’s previous $175 billion outlook, reflecting delays in third-party computing capacity rather than a broader retreat from its AI investment strategy.

Despite the massive expenditures, Microsoft remains highly profitable. The company reported Wednesday that quarterly revenue climbed 19% to $92.3 billion, while net income increased 32% to $36.6 billion.

Microsoft’s Azure cloud business, which provides much of the computing infrastructure used by businesses developing and deploying AI applications, recorded revenue growth of 48%. The company also generated $58 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, although free cash flow totaled $18.6 billion after substantial infrastructure investments.

Meanwhile, shares of Google parent Alphabet plunged Thursday after the company reported negative quarterly free cash flow of $9.1 billion amid mounting AI infrastructure spending and weaker-than-expected advertising revenue.

Microsoft’s financing strategy also reflects its strong standing in credit markets. The company is one of only two publicly traded U.S. corporations holding the highest possible credit ratings from both Moody’s Ratings and S&P Global Ratings, alongside Johnson & Johnson, according to Bloomberg.

The planned offering includes eight fixed-rate tranches and two floating-rate tranches, with JPMorgan Chase, UBS Group and Wells Fargo managing the sale. The longest-dated bonds are expected to mature in 2066, extending Microsoft’s potential repayment obligations four decades into the future.

The debt offering follows Microsoft’s announcement Monday that approximately 60,000 employees would be eligible for voluntary buyouts as the company adjusts its workforce amid its expanding AI investments.

Microsoft confirmed the offers to the Daily Caller News Foundation, which previously reported on the initiative. The company expects no more than 5% of eligible employees to accept the offers, according to its earnings disclosures.

During Wednesday’s earnings call, Bank of America analyst Tal Liani pressed Hood on the company’s financing strategy, asking whether Microsoft intended to raise capital through debt, equity or other funding arrangements.

Hood pointed to the company’s existing use of leasing arrangements and its ability to access debt markets, stressing that Microsoft’s financial position provides multiple financing options.

“We feel good that the return on every dollar of CapEx we’re spending, we’re confident in that,” Hood said. “And therefore, we feel like we have lots of options to be able to tap the financing markets when they make sense and they’re attractive.”
news.content:

news.originalContent:
کریستا پایک، زندانی زن محکوم به اعدام در ایالت تنسی آمریکا که بیش از یک ماه پیش، از تزریق دو دوز داروی کشنده جان سالم به در برد، اولین بیانیه عمومی خود را منتشر کرده است.

او در این بیانیه گفته است که از آن زمان، حتی یک لحظه هم نبوده که درد جسمانی یا روحی نکشیده باشد.

خانم پایک پس از ناکامی مقام‌های زندان در اجرای حکم اعدامش، به بیمارستان منتقل و بعداً مرخص شد. در جریان تلاش برای اجرای حکم، دو دوز از داروی پنتوباربیتال به او تزریق شده بود، اما او زنده ماند.

خانم پایک روز جمعه در بیانیه‌ای که اعضای تیم حقوقی او در شبکه‌های اجتماعی منتشر کردند، گفت بدنش، بازوهایش، دست‌هایش و گلویش درد می‌کند و به‌سختی می‌تواند صحبت کند.

پرونده او و روند اجرای حکم اعدامش باعث انتقاد شدید طرفداران و مخالفان مجازات اعدام شد.

کریستا پایک از سی سال قبل به دلیل قتل و شکنجه کالین اسلمر، یکی از همکلاسی‌هایش، در انتظار اجرای حکم اعدام بوده است.

هنوز مشخص نیست که آیا ایالت تنسی آمریکا قصد دارد در آینده حکم اعدام او را اجرا کند یا نه.

خانم پایک حالا پنجاه ساله است و به همان زندانی بازگردانده شده که طی سی سال اخیر در آن حبس بوده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

گمان می‌رود او تنها فردی باشد که از تلاش برای اعدام از طریق تزریق داروی کشنده جان به در برده است.

پیش‌تر، وکلای خانم پایک گفته بودند که او پس از آنکه از تلاش برای اعدام جان به در برد، به ذات‌الریه مبتلا شده، بازوهایش به‌شدت ورم کرده و توانایی بلعیدن را نیز از دست داده است.

او در بیانیه‌اش گفته است: «در حال بهبودی هستم و می‌دانم که روزبه‌روز قوی‌تر می‌شوم؛ اما بهبودی به معنای آن نیست که خوبم.»

خانم پایک در سال ۱۹۹۶ به جرم قتل کالین اسلمر، زن ۱۹ ساله‌ای که یک سال پیش‌تر کشته شده بود، به اعدام محکوم شد. او هنگام ارتکاب قتل ۱۸ سال داشت.

اجرای حکم کریستا پایک تا آخرین ساعات با کشمکش حقوقی همراه بود. دادگاه تجدیدنظر حوزه ششم آمریکا حدود یک ساعت پیش از زمان تعیین‌شده، اجرای حکم را متوقف کرد، اما چند ساعت بعد دیوان عالی ایالات متحده این توقف را لغو کرد و راه برای اجرای حکم باز شد.

بر اساس اسناد پرونده، خانم پایک و دوست‌پسرش در آن زمان، تاداریل شیپ، در سال ۱۹۹۵ کالین اسلمر را که در یک مرکز آموزش شغلی در ناکسویل با او آشنا شده بودند، مورد ضرب‌وشتم قرار دادند و او را کشتند.

می مارتینز، مادر مقتول، از جمله کسانی بود که خواهان اجرای حکم اعدام کریستا پایک بوده است.

این دومین بار در سال جاری میلادی بود که ایالت تنسی نتوانست یک حکم اعدام را اجرا کند. در ماه مه هم اجرای حکم تونی کاروترز پس از آن متوقف شد که مأموران نتوانستند مسیر وریدی برای تزریق پیدا کنند.

پس از آنکه روند اجرای حکم اعدام خانم پایک با مشکل مواجه شد، وکلای او درخواست فوری برای توقف اعدام و ارائه مراقبت‌های پزشکی ثبت کردند.
